General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gameinformer ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Void/Breaker Review – Chaos Is The Point

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1007 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Many games tout impressive destruction systems under the hood, but few implement it as well as Void/Breaker.
  • Void/Breaker wastes no time getting a gun in your hand.
  • This narrative framework supports the game’s roguelite structure.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Many games tout impressive destruction systems under the hood, but few implement it as well as Void/Breaker. The ruin is visually spectacular, sure – who doesn’t love to watch buildings crumble because of your grenade or gravity-thrown explosives? But importantly, it’s a critical aspect of Void/Breaker’s roguelite design. Enemies caught beneath falling rubble become instantly staggered, and that’s your moment to kill. Grenades do this too, as do most items you throw at the hostile AI machinery trying to end your run, creating a vortex of shifting priorities as you dash, jump, and shoot at sequential staggered enemies in your sightlines. Countless weapon mods and permutations make fewer than a dozen weapons feel like hundreds in your arsenal, adding even more blissful chaos to the mix. Though it can be difficult at times, if you can see through the literal remains of your destruction, one of the year’s most engaging shooters awaits.

Void/Breaker wastes no time getting a gun in your hand. An AI voice in your head wants your help escaping a simulation where thousands of runners attempt to reach the end of multi-arena stages to defeat a boss. He asks that you simply follow the simulation’s commands; meanwhile, he uses the data you collect along the way to find upcoming exits for you and him. The storytelling style is very reminiscent of Valve’s Portal. Something much larger is at play here, but it’s worth discovering for yourself.

This narrative framework supports the game’s roguelite structure. Mechanically, however, you enter various themed digital stages, from liminal spaces to beaches to snow-capped cliffs and more, and attempt to survive. Most arenas consist of a couple of starkly white structures that your grenades and thrown explosives can topple (ideally onto waves of enemies below). Learning the language of Void/Breaker means constantly scanning your field of view for explosives and structures practically begging to come down, and then eyeing neon-green bars above enemies that tell you they’re staggered and ready for a quick kill. Developer Stubby Games throws plenty of wrenches into this formula, like armored foes and electrostatic enemies you must melee first, and elite bots that will have you on the back foot, but for the most part, Void/Breaker’s formula is “Break stuff, then kill.”.

The game emphasizes explosives and bringing buildings down, but your guns do most of the killing; you can only select one weapon per run. You choose from a pistol, shotgun, machine gun, sniper, and more, and each has its perks (though once I unlocked the SMG, I rarely picked anything else). There’s no sense overthinking your weapon, though, because the dozens of mods you pick up each run determine its effectiveness. As you pick up more schematics, the pool of mods you find in chests or drop from enemies expands, and soon your gun fires corrosive acid, electricity, fire, projectile missiles, and more. Not to mention, mods change how the gun fires, how much damage certain bullets do, recoil, accuracy, and just about any other stat you associate with firing a video game gun. Wild combinations are easy to create, and a unique mod-stacking mechanic that can double or triple effectiveness adds a light touch of puzzle design to this otherwise straight shooter.

Stubby Games smartly emphasizes player expression, never getting in the way of the zanier combinations available to players. The SMG I used to beat the final boss featured mods that made each bullet electric, shot missiles with each shot, covered each bullet in a destructive orb, and featured a ricochet perk that made each bullet bounce off walls and split into even more bullets. I’m thankful for mid-run saves because this SMG permutation, paired with an ability mod that let me throw infinite grenades for a limited time, filled my screen with so much destruction that the entire game crashed. I’d usually bemoan such a thing, but I couldn’t help but laugh. I pushed my PC to its limit with my on-screen chaos.

Boss fights leave a little to be desired – I rarely died because of their simple bullet-hell arenas. Instead, most runs ended because, after bringing down every structure around me, I’d get so lost in the chaos that I wouldn't realize I was stuck in debris while enemies swarmed my location. As stunning as it is to see so much happening on screen, it can be hard to understand what is going on during the most chaotic moments.

In a recent development, between enemy-filled arenas en route to a stage’s end boss, you might find a shop to buy more mods, ominous obelisks with risk-reward propositions (gain a lot of health or lose half your health, for example), optional trials, and strange phenomena that transport you to different locations. These moments are quick breaks in between bouts of adrenaline-fueled shooter action that I always welcomed – enemies can be relentless, especially as new types are introduced in each stage.

Industry observers note that the rest of the Void/Breaker package offers few genre surprises. You can upgrade various traits between runs, research new mod schematics to add to the random pool, purchase new weapons, and discover fun secrets. You can unlock shortcuts, glean in-world information from computer terminals, and hear intriguing dialogue barks from the AI partner who needs your help. It’s all standard stuff for the rogue genre, but if anything, its simplicity pushes you back to the meat and potatoes of this shooter.

Industry observers note that void/Breaker’s shorter runtime – I rolled credits at 12 hours – ensures nothing gets too repetitive in its roguelite structure, but an expansive endgame promises even more to engage with, like different run modifications you can enable to make an already chaotic shooter even more anarchic. I’ll certainly be running it back (again and again) to see what other disruptions I can bring to this AI-simulated adventure. It’s hard not to when destruction feels this good.

Industry observers note that bad signal or dead zones? Download your issues before you leave and read anywhere.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that here’s a fun fact: in the lore of the Fallout series, dogs weren’t allowed into the Vault-Tec Vaults, with all the dogs we see throughout the games being those that survived and evolved into wolf-like forms after the Great War.
  • Recent findings suggest that A newly-discovered document from the Australian Classification Board has leaked the existence of a new Fallout spin-off game titled A Wasteland Full of Cats.
  • According to recent reports, is it the Fallout game we’ve all been waiting for in the near-decade since the launch of Fallout 76?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that here’s a fun fact: in the lore of the Fallout series, dogs weren’t allowed into the Vault-Tec Vaults, with all the dogs we see throughout the games being those that survived and evolved into wolf-like forms after the Great War. Cats, on the other hand, were permitted into the Vaults within reason thanks to their applications as therapy pets and efficacy as pest-hunters. In spite of that, cats didn’t start appearing in the Fallout games until Fallout 4 and Fallout 76. Apparently, the reason for that is that they all just sorta got lost somewhere.

Recent findings suggest that A newly-discovered document from the Australian Classification Board has leaked the existence of a new Fallout spin-off game titled A Wasteland Full of Cats. This game is apparently being created in cooperation between Bethesda and Devcats, an indie developer specializing in hidden object games about cats like A Park Full of Cats, A Building Full of Cats, and An Arcade Full of Cats.

According to recent reports, is it the Fallout game we’ve all been waiting for in the near-decade since the launch of Fallout 76? No, definitely not, but, well, it’s something, I suppose. Every bit of Fallout-adjacent content we get can continue to tide us over until Fallout 5, whenever that ends up being, or at least the next season of the Fallout television series.

It has been revealed that according to the description of the game on the Australian Classification Board website, A Wasteland Full of Cats will cast you in the role of one of the various cats living in one of the Vaults that dot the Wasteland. Following some manner of accident, all of the other cats living in the Vault alongside you are let loose out into the Wasteland, and you’ll need to go out there to round them all up.

In the same vein as Devcats’s other games, this will be a jaunt through 14 locations and 33 rooms where you’ll need to point out the errant cats hidden within the scenery, Where’s Waldo-style.

A Wasteland Full of Cats will cast you in the role of one of the various cats living in one of the Vaults.

It has been revealed that you’ll be helped along the way by various NPC characters, hopefully including some familiar faces, with many of the locations you visit apparently being classic spots from across the Fallout franchise. Some of these locations will have mild puzzle elements, allowing you to uncover non-critical secret levels. According to the description, the game will culminate in a final battle against a horde of Radroaches, though I’m admittedly not quite sure how finding cats translates into battling giant mutant roaches, but I guess we’ll find out.

It has been an exceptionally hot minute since the last mainline Fallout game, specifically the release of Fallout 4 in 2015. Since then, it’s been pretty much exclusively spin-offs, such as the mobile title Fallout Shelter, its gacha-added version, Fallout Shelter Online, the MMO stylings of Fallout 76, and I guess Zen Pinball’s Fallout table for the Pinball FX games, if you want to count that.

It has been revealed that back in 2022, Todd Howard said in an interview with IGN that development on Fallout 5 would begin in earnest once The Elder Scrolls VI was done and dusted. Of course, considering we only just learned that game’s full title recently, I have a sinking feeling the timeline has shifted on that a bit. For what it’s worth, Bethesda did say in an X, formerly Twitter post this past July that Fallout 5 has officially begun pre-production, but again, that doesn’t give us much to go on.

Sources indicate that as of now, we don’t have any particular release dates or even release windows for upcoming Fallout projects, whether it’s mainline games, the TV show, or even this fresh cat thing. Just gotta keep wading through the Wasteland patiently, I guess….

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A fresh Arc Raiders patch has arrived, bringing a host of new fixes to several exploits players have recently been relying on to do things they’re not supposed to, and bypass certain mechanics to get into areas without having to go through proper channels.

The patch is fairly small, and surprisingly doesn’t include any buffs or nerfs to anything in particular.

In a recent development, the list of notes for revision 1.4.0 is compact, with a clear focus on addressing several exploits. The biggest one, of course, is the addition of “exploit mitigation mechanisms” to stop players from glitching through locked doors.

Industry observers note that this fix applies to all maps, and it’s intended to address an issue whereby players would not bring the required keys to access those areas of the various maps. Locked rooms, if they can be unlocked, often hide a wealth of high-tier and rare loot.

But players have also been using similar exploits to clip through walls and access areas outside the playspace, allowing them to ambush enemy players and set up traps that would be impossible for others to detect.

In a recent development, the game’s recent patch, which was released exactly one week ago, mainly consisted of balance tweaks to some of the more popular weapons and mines. However, it also introduced a few fixes to prevent players from clipping through walls by using barricades.

While on the subject of being in places where you’re not supposed to, the patch blocked exterior access to the locked room inside Spaceport's Control Tower, making it only accessible from inside the tower.

1.4.0 also fixes an especially nasty exploit that allowed players to bring up their weapons much faster than normal by promptly swapping to the quick use menu. There’s a range of smaller fixes for lighting and texture bugs here, too, and you can read all about it in the full change log below:.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you’re in downtown Los Angeles now through November 29 and want to get an up-close-and-personal look at some cool cars, head over to the convention center to see what’s poppin’ at the annual auto show.
  • It’s one thing to see the Tesla Roadster through your smartphone screen; it’s another thing to see it about six feet away.
  • Recent findings suggest that being in the same room as a Bugatti EB110 is about as common as being in the same room as Sir Anthony Hopkins.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’re in downtown Los Angeles now through November 29 and want to get an up-close-and-personal look at some cool cars, head over to the convention center to see what’s poppin’ at the annual auto show. However, if you don’t have time to make the trip—or you’re nowhere near L.A.—and want to see the best cars that this year’s event had to offer, we've got you covered. While the 2026 L.A. auto show was short on major debuts or futuristic concepts, it hosted several headline-catching cars as well as multiple highly anticipated new models.

It’s one thing to see the Tesla Roadster through your smartphone screen; it’s another thing to see it about six feet away. While we’re highly skeptical that Tesla will ever publicly sell the thruster-equipped version that flew through the air and did a barrel roll, it’s more likely that a similar-looking, street-legal version will eventually reach production. Haters gonna hate, but the Roadster looks pretty damn cool, like Lamborghini designer Fabrizio Giugiaro was hired to style his version of the Lotus Esprit S1 that James Bond drove in The Spy Who Loved Me. Consider us shaken, not stirred.

Recent findings suggest that being in the same room as a Bugatti EB110 is about as common as being in the same room as Sir Anthony Hopkins. Like meeting the actor who famously played Hannibal Lecter, meeting one of the most iconic supercars ever made is unnerving. Now, you may have noticed that this example isn’t exactly all original; instead, it has been modified by Phiaro Inc., and it features a custom widebody kit as well as a chameleon-like paint job. The best part? Its modifications are completely reversible. Let’s just say it drew a crowd.

Genesis is going after the throats of luxury stalwarts like BMW, Mercedes-Benz and—dare we say—Bentley with the new GV90. The one you see here is the top-of-the-line Neolun model, and its most distinctive feature is these gigantic coach doors. Inside are four VIP-grade seats that treat passengers to an opulent cabin awash in rich materials and front seats that swivel 180 degrees to create a mobile lounge (this configuration is only accessible when the 657-hp EV is parked). The GV90 Neolun also has a veneer wood floor and 24-inch wheels that remind us of the iconic monoblock wheels made famous by Mercedes-AMG and Brabus. Few SUVs turn our heads, but Genesis appears to have another game-changer on its metaphorical hands.

Toyota Crown Signia GT-S Concept.

We spotted this beautiful wagon-like Toyota Crown Signia from across the convention center’s south hall. Among a sea of generic crossovers, this low-slung longroof is an ode to an age when most Americans didn’t lust after the elevated seating position of a semi-truck. Of course, if you haven’t noticed, this isn’t exactly a production-spec Crown Signia. If you read our recent SEMA coverage, you may recognize it as the GT-S concept. Along with being lowered by five inches and wearing flared fenders that resemble the Mustang GTD, it has custom one-off coil-over dampers, 21-inch HRE wheels, and brakes from a Lexus RX500h F Sport. To all that, we say, “Hell yeah, brother!”.

Let’s take a break from the world of flying cars, Bugattis, and fanciful electric SUVs to enjoy something that most people can afford: the upcoming eighth-generation Hyundai Elantra. If its disorienting front lighting, heavily creased bodywork, and broad haunches intimidate you, we’re sure there’s a safer-looking alternative in Toyota’s showroom. But whatever you may think about the new Elantra’s styling, it definitely attracts attention. And Hyundai is hoping it’ll do just that to new customers who are looking to join the brand’s family tree. The nonhybrid version seen here draws power from a humble 147-hp four-cylinder engine, but the lineup will add a more powerful hybrid model sometime next year. While pricing is still TBD, we expect that it’ll cost around $25,000 to own the most interesting car in your cul-de-sac.

Ram 1500 Rumble Bee Foose Edition.

According to recent reports, if you’ve ever watched an episode of Overhaulin’, a TV show that lasted for 10 seasons on TLC, then you’ve heard of custom car designer Chip Foose. Now, he has teamed up with Fox Factory Vehicles to create this even more muscular version of the new Ram 1500 Rumble Bee street truck. Along with unique wheels and body graphics, the interior has been restyled with diamond-stitched seats and Foose branding. The truck itself has a lowered ride height with an aftermarket coil-over suspension, and its supercharged V-8 is available with either 705 or 1000 horsepower. That’s a lot of horsies, and they’ll cost customers a lot of cash, with the Rumble Bee Foose Edition starting at $154,990.

It has been revealed that this was one of the few concept cars at the show, but the Acura Nexera was first revealed back in August during Monterey Car Week. Still, the futuristic concept is really cool to see in person, especially with its dramatic glass canopy. Plus, how many times have you seen an Acura with butterfly doors? While the Nexera doesn’t preview an upcoming production model, it does provide a glimpse of Acura’s next-generation design language. Will the new 2028 RDX feature an active rear spoiler, carbon-fiber accents, and lighting that glows through the bodywork? Probably not. However, we can expect to see some of the Nexera concept’s interesting styling influence the brand’s next-gen compact SUV.

Acura Integra Type S Heritage Edition.

If you’re old enough to remember Acura’s legendary DC2 Integra Type R, you’ll definitely appreciate this new Integra Type S Heritage Edition. Not only does its Blazing Phoenix Yellow call more attention to itself than Significant Bird starring in an old-timey picture show, but it also honors the OG Type R, which also wore a shade of Phoenix Yellow. The modern-day throwback sport compact packs the same 320-hp turbo four and six-speed manual as other models, but this one alone has copper-colored wheels and a titanium shift knob from the Honda Civic Type R. To get one in your driveway, you’ll need to be lucky enough to score one of the 700 limited copies for the U.S. market, but the asking price is a reasonable $58,995.

It has been revealed that have you been waiting for Dodge to stuff a Hemi V-8 in the newly introduced Charger? Well, you’re going to have to keep waiting for a while. However, if you’ve been hoping that the Brotherhood of Muscle will make a gas-powered Charger that’s set up for quick lap times, the new Super Bee variant should help you scratch that itch. Along with exclusive aero bits, stronger brakes, and wider summer tires, this track-focused Charger features an enhanced high-output Hurricane twin-turbo 3.0-liter straight-six, which is good for 600 horsepower (50 more than normal). The reimagined “Super Bee” logo on the rear quarter panel is one way to separate it from its siblings, but it also has an entirely different front clip that features new headlights and more open space to inhale engine-cooling air. If you’re wondering how much it costs, so are we, so stay tuned.

Industry observers note that like many of you, this was our first time seeing the fresh Chevy Silverado 1500’s new off-road-focused ZR2 variant. It’s a significant truck, so big that we initially thought it was the HD version. Among the many changes to the newest generation of Chevy’s bestselling full-size pickup truck are all-new small-block V-8s. The ZR2 seen here is powered by a 481-hp 6.6-liter that helps churn massive all-terrain tires, which now stand 35 inches tall for the first time on a half-ton Silverado. The Ford F-150 Raptor-rivaling ZR2’s other party tricks include trick Multimatic DSSV spool-valve dampers. Inside, it includes GM’s first use of forged carbon fiber (neat!). If you want the most badass version, you’ll want to opt for the Bison Edition that adds beadlock-capable wheels, unique bumpers, and even more underbody armor. The cost of admission for the regular ZR2 is just under $80K, while the Bison starts even higher.

According to recent reports, eric Stafford’s automobile addiction began before he could walk, and it has fueled his passion to write news, reviews, and more for Car and Driver since 2016. His aspiration growing up was to become a millionaire with a Jay Leno–like car collection. Apparently, getting rich is harder than social-media influencers make it seem, so he avoided financial success entirely to become an automotive journalist and drive upcoming cars for a living. After earning a journalism degree at Central Michigan University and working at a daily newspaper, the years of basically burning money on failed project cars and lemon-flavored jalopies finally paid off when Car and Driver hired him. His garage presently includes a 2010 Acura RDX, a manual '97 Chevy Camaro Z/28, and a '90 Honda CRX Si.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The R2 comes with fixed suspension, so the driver has to be very careful when choosing their lines, but thankfully, there are now a handful of companies out there that sell suspension lift kits for the R2.
  • Sources indicate that bullray Manufacturing made a custom lift kit for a Rivian R2 that’s used as a chase truck for the Off Grid racing team.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the Rivian R2 may be a little tamer than its bigger brothers, the R1S and R1T, but that doesn’t mean that the aftermarket world can’t chime in and lend a helping hand. While the mid-size SUV carried over many of its larger siblings’ characteristics, it lacks one feature that could make the difference between getting back home the same day and spending hours trying to get unstuck: adjustable air suspension.

The R2 comes with fixed suspension, so the driver has to be very careful when choosing their lines, but thankfully, there are now a handful of companies out there that sell suspension lift kits for the R2.

Sources indicate that bullray Manufacturing made a custom lift kit for a Rivian R2 that’s used as a chase truck for the Off Grid racing team. The electric SUV, an R2 Performance, made an appearance at this year’s SEMA show in Las Vegas and was filmed by Out of Spec Bits.

The 2.0-inch metal lifters were fitted above the dampers, and the electric crossover retains its standard semi-active suspension. In other words, this is a body lift, not a suspension lift, but it shouldn’t matter too much, considering this is a unibody vehicle, after all. The high-voltage battery and electric motors are fitted directly to the underside of the body, so the added ground clearance should help protect vital components when going off the beaten track.

It’s also worth noting that EV Sportline, a manufacturer that specializes in aftermarket parts for electric vehicles, offers a 1.6-inch body lift kit for the Rivian R2.

Sources indicate that getting back to the green R2 that went to SEMA, it’s obvious that it’s fully kitted out for any overlanding experience. There’s a Baja Designs 40-inch light bar, a set of Maxtrax Extreme recovery boards, plenty of storage options on the roof, and a Rig’D tire carrier at the rear. A set of Yokohama Geolandar Mud-Terrain tires wrapped around 17-inch Method Racing wheels completes the look.

Inside, there’s a communications system, as well as a racing-spec GPS navigation system for the front passenger.

All in all, it looks really badass and shows that there’s a lot of potential in the aftermarket space for the Rivian R2. Clearly, the raised ride height and chunky tires will eat into the car’s official 330-mile range, but that’s to be expected.

It has been revealed that aurora Gaming came from a map down to beat F9 EICAR 2-1 and win the first VCT EMEA Kickoff Europe open qualifier. The win came days after they were put back into the bracket when the UK team BONK was disqualified for cheating.

Recent findings suggest that the VCT EMEA Kickoff: Europe Qualifier 2027 decider got under way at 18:45. The series began on Lotus. Aurora’s chiwa was named most valuable player of the series.

Sources indicate that the Aurora roster lists Boo, chiwa, Derke, B1SK and trexx. F9 EICAR, based in France, fielded Kipperman, Destrian, Tenshi, izana and Geekkooo.

In a recent development, aurora’s run nearly ended early. BONK, a UK Valorant roster, beat them 2-1 in the round of 32 on 6 November. That result followed a comeback from 3-11 down on Bind. Riot’s ruling against BONK reversed Aurora’s exit. Every BONK player and registered team member was provisionally suspended. Project 100K and ycatble returned to the bracket along with Aurora.

Industry observers note that the qualifier left no room for error. It was a single-elimination bracket for 256 teams, and every match was a best-of-three. Once reinstated, Aurora did not drop a map before the final. They beat Pixel Lumina 2-0 in the second semi-final.

Recent findings suggest that in the first semi-final, xXxMasterProMegaTeamxXx fell 2-1 to F9 EICAR. The French side had arrived at the qualifier in mixed form. F9 EICAR lost 0-2 to WIP Esports in VCL France: Revolution Stage 2 2026 and were twice beaten 1-2 by Mandatory. A 2-1 result against Esprit Shōnen was their only victory in that run.

Recent findings suggest that the Elo power rankings show the gap on paper. F9 EICAR sit at rank 241, with a rating of 1405 and a 6-16 record in 22 rated matches. Aurora are unranked.

It has been revealed that the final still carried weight. Seeding for the playoff stage would be decided by the result, Insider Gaming reported.

It has been revealed that the stakes are clear. Under Riot’s 2027 system, four non-partner teams will reach VCT EMEA Kickoff. Two will come from Europe, one from Türkiye and one from the Middle East and North Africa.

— Aurora Valorant (@Aurora_Valorant) November 10, 2026.

Sources indicate that that leaves European hopefuls chasing places at a 12-team LAN event. VCT 2027 EMEA Kickoff will be run by Riot Games at the Riot Games Arena in Berlin.

The playoff field is not yet complete. The top four teams from each open qualifier move on, and the second Europe open qualifier is set for 12 to 15 November. The playoffs will use a modified double-elimination bracket of best-of-three matches, with a best-of-five grand final. The top two finishers earn places at VCT 2027 EMEA Kickoff, whose window runs from 14 January to 7 February.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Red Bull Formula 1 team has a brutal reputation for chewing up promising new drivers, but Kiwi driver Liam Lawson has kept his focus after being demoted from being Max Verstappen’s teammate back to the junior Visa Cash App Racing Bulls (VCARB) team in 2025. Lawson had an excellent year with the Racing Bulls so far, including a top-10 finish and a respectable stand-in back at Red Bull over the summer filling in for an injured Isack Hadjar.

Despite his performance, he was unsure of his seat for 2027 until just a few days ago, when VCARB confirmed Lawson and teammate Arvid Lindblad will both return for next year. Discussion of the future was still off limits for this interview, but it was a noticeably relaxed Liam Lawson who sat down with us to talk about significant trucks, sad songs, and what makes Vegas such a tough race.

Car and Driver: What is the week leading up to a race like, especially a media-heavy one like Las Vegas?

See all results for used cars for sale near 47712.

Liam Lawson: Vegas is a unique race in many aspects. The timings of it [Vegas is a night race]. And then this weekend for us, this year in general with these cars, there were new regulations, new power units. Every weekend has been a bit of a challenge to learn. Vegas is very cold and not high grip, it's very, very low grip. The track’s quite dirty as well. They open the street up at night and it sort of makes it quite difficult for us when we come back the next day. So the prep that goes in is a little bit more than normal. We’re definitely doing a lot on the simulator side.

Do you guys have a way to do simulator work on the road, not just sort of between races?

Sources indicate that oh, no, unfortunately not. It’s back at base Milton Keynes. So for a triple header like this [Vegas, Qatar, Abu Dhabi], we will do time on all three tracks before and get them basically dialed and then go to the races, but we don’t have time to go back in between races, unfortunately.

It has been revealed that I guess I hadn’t really thought of it that way, but because the setup is so different, even tracks that you’re very familiar with are going to be almost like upcoming tracks. Like each race you’re all running for the first time with this setup.

Yeah, it’s very different, especially at the start of the year. I would say things are now getting a lot more consistent as we get in the groove of things. It's been tricky and we’ve just been learning through the year and the cars have been getting a lot better as well as we bring upgrades. It’s been a lot busier. We started probably in January, a lot earlier than normal with preseason testing and trying to get a handle on these cars.

Recent findings suggest that you’re known as a pretty technical guy, a pretty technical driver. What’s your relationship with your team in terms of giving them feedback on the cars or being involved in setup?

See all results for used cars for sale near 47712.

It’s very different depending on driver. I think it’s vital the relationship you have with your engineers, that they understand the type of driver that you are as well, because, the way that you give feedback sometimes can be misheard, you know, or like misunderstood. My relationship with the guys I work with has strengthened a lot through the year. Alex [race engineer Alexandre Iliopoulos], when I’m speaking about something, he knows pretty much what I’m saying and understands it.

Every driver is different. I would definitely say I’m more invested on the technical side as well, especially on the development side of the car. And the direction that we’ve been going in through the year where we’ve been trying to improve the car-specific areas. I’ve been a little bit lucky as well that I got to drive a couple of different cars as well in the past and obviously this year as well.

What’s the feedback process after a session?

It’s something that is different for everybody, but when we come in from a session, we basically sit in a major circle and the specific roles on the team go through their individual feedback on the session. I talk about what I feel in the car and report that back. And then I talk about the main things that I need from the car to be quicker in the next sessions.

You sound very comfortable with that. Another important part of your guys’ job, especially in the last few years as F1 has become so much more mainstream, is social media. How do you like that kind of stuff? How do you deal with it? Do you think it’s fun? Do you hate it?

In a recent development, probably somewhere in the middle, I would say. I don’t mind it sometimes, as long as it’s not in the way of performance. That’s what we’re all focused on. But it’s been good. I mean, the sport is in a great place and the support we have as drivers now is growing every year. We see that at all the races we go to, especially in the U.S. It’s been incredible to see. Very cool. So it’s mostly positive. And some of it can be quite fun to do.

In a recent development, do you like the ones where they hit you with quiz questions? Or do you want to do little dance moves? What’s your favorite kind of social post?

[laughs] Definitely not doing little dance moves. The sort of question games that I’ll sit down with Arvid and do are good. The ones that take the least amount of time, they’re probably the ones that I enjoy doing the most on a race weekend. But we’ve done some cool stuff outside of track as well, and at some recent races with the team like doing a [musical] performance recently in Austin.

Oh let’s talk about that! You’re a musician as well as a driver.

Sources indicate that guitar. That’s something I’ve done since I was very young. My parents had me playing and learning classical guitar. Now I just play for fun, mostly like country music.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a fair amount of you guys who play instruments. Could you put an all-F1 band together? Doesn’t Charles play piano?

Yeah, Lewis is very good as well.

Industry observers note that I have no idea. I don’t think anybody plays drums. It’s either guitar or piano but I would say most of the grid is not musically gifted.

In a recent development, back to cars. Is there any street car that you really like to drive?

Yeah, and it’s really only in the U.S. I get to drive it just ’cause it’s so substantial that it doesn’t fit in Europe or anywhere else in the world. At the moment I drive a Ford Raptor R. I drove here today from California, from Newport Beach. It’s the ultimate daily. It’s kind of got everything. It’s very high horsepower. It’s got basically Trophy Truck suspension, and it’s comfortable as well. It’s just not very good on fuel, so it’s definitely expensive to fill up during the day.

Sources indicate that what, they don’t give you a fuel card at Visa Cash App, Liam? Next time you do that drive, you can actually drive from Los Angeles to Las Vegas pretty much all off-road.

Sources indicate that what? Really? I’d be very interested to do that because that’s like what this truck is made for.

Any other hobbies besides jumping Raptors and playing country music?

I ride dirt bikes. I’ve got a track that I built in Fresh Zealand at home. I have a KTM 250. It’s probably not something the team loves.

According to recent reports, yeah, mostly motocross. The track I have at home, it’s not too crazy. It’s on the safer side, you know, I would say it doesn’t have any like crazy doubles or stuff.

Are you telling me that or are you telling your manager in the background?

Okay, last question, what’s your favorite country music song?

“Whiskey Glasses,” Morgan Wallen.

Like a sleeper agent activated late in the game, Elana Scherr didn’t know her calling at a young age. Like many girls, she planned to be a vet-astronaut-artist, and came closest to that last one by attending UCLA art school. She painted images of cars, but did not own one. Elana reluctantly got a driver’s license at age 21 and discovered that she not only loved cars and wanted to drive them, but that other people loved cars and wanted to read about them, which meant somebody had to write about them. Since receiving activation codes, Elana has written for numerous car magazines and websites, covering classics, car culture, technology, motorsports, and new-car reviews. In 2020, she received a Best Feature award from the Motor Press Guild for the C/D story "A Drive through Classic Americana in a Polestar 2."  In 2023, her Car and Driver feature story "In Washington, D.C.'s Secret Carpool Cabal, It's a Daily Slug Fest" was awarded 1st place in the 16th Annual National Arts & Entertainment Journalism Awards by the Los Angeles Press Club.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, forget waiting in line for a discounted TV or other gadget you probably don’t need.
  • While electric vehicle sales have slowed in the US after last year’s rush of buyers trying to claim the $7,500 tax credit before it expired, the market is bouncing back.
  • Nearly 263,000 EVs were sold in the US in the third quarter, according to Kelley Blue Book, marking the most since the record-setting third quarter of 2025.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, forget waiting in line for a discounted TV or other gadget you probably don’t need. If you’ve been looking to go electric, Black Friday may be the time to do it. Several brands, including Kia, Lucid, and Volkswagen, are offering $10,000 or more off select EVs right now.

While electric vehicle sales have slowed in the US after last year’s rush of buyers trying to claim the $7,500 tax credit before it expired, the market is bouncing back.

Nearly 263,000 EVs were sold in the US in the third quarter, according to Kelley Blue Book, marking the most since the record-setting third quarter of 2025.

It has been revealed that with new models hitting the market, prices have also come down over the past year. The average transaction price (ATP) for a new EV in October was $56,221, down 2.9% from a year ago.

For Black Friday, several automakers are sweetening the deal this year, offering a generous $10,000 or more off select EVs.

Industry observers note that lucid introduced its Black Friday offers this week. Through November 30, you can score a $15,000 Black Friday Credit on a upcoming 2027 Lucid Gravity Touring.

Recent findings suggest that prefer a sedan? Lucid is also offering a $10,000 Black Friday Credit on a new 2027 Lucid Air Touring. To take advantage of the offer, you must pay cash or use third-party financing.

The 2027 Lucid Gravity Touring starts at $79,900 and offers up to 337 miles of EPA-estimated range. It’s available to lease for as low as $749 a month. The offer is for a 36-month lease with $6,249 due at signing.

Lucid’s electric sedan, the 2027 Air Touring, is priced from $79,900 and offers up to 431 miles of range.

Both the Gravity and Air can add up to 200 miles of range in under 12 minutes with 400 kW DC fast charging.

Lucid’s Black Friday offers end on November 30, 2026.

Kia is offering $10,000 off several electric vehicles for Black Friday, including the three-row EV9 and the Niro EV.

It has been revealed that the 2026 Kia EV9 is available with a $10,000 Customer Cash discount that can be applied toward the purchase price. With a $10,000 discount, prices for the base EV9 Light RWD trim can fall to as low as $44,900 ($54,900 starting MSRP).

Kia is also promoting a lease deal on the 2026 EV9 Light Long Range RWD for $339/month for 36 months, with $4,999 due at signing.

If you opt to finance, you can get 0% APR for 60 months, plus $5,000 in APR Bonus Cash across the entire 2026 EV9 lineup.

The 2026 Kia Niro EV is also available with a $10,000 Customer Cash discount, knocking the price down to as low as $29,700 ($39,700 MSRP).

With leases starting at just $289/month for 36 months (with $3,999 due at signing), the 2026 Niro EV Wind FWD is about as cheap a lease as you can get nowadays, gas or electric.

The Niro EV is also available with 0% APR for up to 72 months, including a $3,500 APR Bonus Cash discount.

While it isn’t $10,000 off, it is worth mentioning that Kia now sells the smaller EV3 electric SUV. The 2027 Kia EV3 (see our review) starts at just $28,890, making it one of the most affordable EVs you can get in the US, alongside the upcoming Chevy Bolt and Nissan LEAF.

Kia is offering a $1,500 Customer Cash discount on the 2027 EV3, which still makes it cheaper to buy outright than the Niro EV, even with incentives.

The 2027 Kia EV3 Wind FWD is available for lease starting at $349/month for 36 months, with $3,999 due at signing. Kia is offering 0.90% APR for 48 months on all 2027 EV3 trims.

Kia’s current deals end on January 04, 2027.

As it prepares to introduce its replacement in 2027, Volkswagen introduced a $10,000 Customer Bonus for the 2026 ID.4 electric SUV.

Industry observers note that since the ID.4 is discontinued after the 2026 model year, it might not be so easy to find one. Volkswagen said the remaining inventory is very limited.

If you can find one, Volkswagen will apply the $10,000 discount when you purchase or lease a new 2026 ID.4 through a participating dealer.

According to recent reports, volkswagen’s current ID.4 offer runs until November 30, 2026. You can read more about its replacement, the ID. Tiguan here.

#17811. 10 Details That Show GTA 6 Deserves Game of the Year

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

10 Details That Show GTA 6 Deserves Game of the Year

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1403 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 is now available to the public, but the controversial part doesn’t have anything to do with the game itself, but rather, what the game has been nominated for.
  • Industry observers note that the nominees for Game of the Year at The Game Awards have officially been announced, and before GTA 6 was available to the public, it was placed as a nominee.
  • According to recent reports, this has obviously bothered many gamers, but there is a reason why GTA 6 is on this list of nominees.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is now available to the public, but the controversial part doesn’t have anything to do with the game itself, but rather, what the game has been nominated for.

Industry observers note that the nominees for Game of the Year at The Game Awards have officially been announced, and before GTA 6 was available to the public, it was placed as a nominee. In fact, it was nominated for more than just Game of the Year.

According to recent reports, this has obviously bothered many gamers, but there is a reason why GTA 6 is on this list of nominees. Let’s break down why this long-awaited title deserves Game of the Year.

Rockstar is known for adding some great music to games. GTA 5 has a pretty great soundtrack, with it featuring numerous artists. Because of that, it was no surprise that Rockstar started announcing various artists for GTA 6.

The radio is stacked with some amazing musicians who took the time to write latest songs specifically for the game. With so much talent, it is difficult not to get lost in the beat, so long as you are someone who enjoys each artist’s music.

In the end, users recognize that this talent isn’t just for show, and the music in GTA 6 fits the vibe of the crime-forward series, making it feel more alive.

People have been waiting 13 years to get their hands on GTA 6. Ever since Grand Theft Auto 5 was released, people have been asking for the next game in the series. Well, over the course of those 13 years, Rockstar has been working hard.

The team has been busting their butts to develop GTA 6 and make it as big as possible. They have talked about how they created upcoming systems, enhanced older ones, and added a ton of detail into their newest game.

With this much effort put in, there is no denying that the team deserves some recognition, and just being nominated demonstrates that people care.

For a long time, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time held the record for being the highest rated game of all time with a 99 on MetaCritic. Now that reviews for GTA 6 are out, it shares the same score as Ocarina of Time.

With that being said, there were 22 professional reviews for Ocarina of Time, and over 150 for GTA 6, so GTA 6 has a more accurate representation from multiple parties, putting it above Ocarina of Time.

In a recent development, that isn’t a fluke. You can look at a few review scores, see a 10/10 and write it off, but when there are over 100 different people giving it the same score or something similar, that isn’t a coincidence.

There are many people, who, when they purchase a game, are in it for the visual aspect. There is nothing wrong with this, and with the advancement of graphics engines, it has become commonplace for games to try and look lifelike.

Industry observers note that grand Theft Auto 6 has some of the best visuals of any game that has been released this year, and even in the last decade. The developers at Rockstar spend a lot of time trying to make every shot look as cinematic as possible.

The result of this, is one of the most beautiful games to come out in a very long time, and it will hold up for many years to come. The only slight downside is the 30fps, but that is a small price to pay for this level of beauty.

According to recent reports, rockstar has spent ages working on GTA 6, and a major part of that work has gone into making the world feel more alive rather than a sandbox that you can run and gun in like it was in GTA 5. Previous titles didn’t respect you being a character in the world, but rather let you do whatever you wanted.

NPCs have received a major overhaul in GTA 6, reacting more to you being in the world, and turning the game into a major life sim where people will get angry with you if you pull a gun, run away in fear, and much more.

Recent findings suggest that in addition to this, there are tons of activities to take part in, so much so that you can ignore the main quest for ages and still have plenty to do. You definitely won’t get bored with this game.

In a recent development, instead of focusing on fleshing out three individual characters, this time around Rockstar decided to focus on creating a couple. Their names are Jason and Lucia, and their story is powerful, and they are far more fleshed out than characters in the previous game.

Jason and Lucia are madly in love, and they will do anything to stand by one another. The Bonnie and Clyde dynamic fits the location of Vice City very well, and it is a story that many didn’t think would work at first.

This type of emphasis on building a relationship is something that we haven’t seen in a while, and Rockstar made it work very well, meaning it is a game that will be remembered for a long time.

Recent findings suggest that rockstar is known for making some incredible characters, and GTA 6 is no exception to this. From the beginning to the end, there are numerous characters that you meet that have a lasting effect on the story and some that are only there for a moment but leave an impression.

Industry observers note that think about your time with GTA 5 and how it was fun interacting with the game’s characters. They made you laugh, and they certainly are remembered.

Well, GTA 6 has that and then some, with a cast of side characters that each have a standout personality that will make you remember them for some time to come. It shows that the devs knew what they were doing when creating the world of Leonida.

According to recent reports, if there is something that the Rockstar devs understand it is comedy. There was so much of it baked into GTA 5 that it was difficult to avoid. Now that same energy has been carried over to GTA 6 and it is fantastic.

If you are a fan of satire then be prepared to see it everywhere in GTA 6 because nearly everything is a satirical take on a organization, person, or event.

Rockstar devs are masters of comedic timing and satire, and GTA 6 proves it. It is a game that will have you chuckling at the references and laughing at the absurdity. It hits the funny bone and there is no denying that that plays a major role in why it is so good.

Industry observers note that something that I like in games is when you can edit your character in some way. I like to make my own character or dress up existing characters in fun outfits, and GTA 6 has that and then some.

Similar to previous games in the series, there are numerous outfits that you can purchase for your characters, which is a dream for those who like to customize their look. On top of that, you can edit your cars, and you can also edit your appearance through working out.

That’s right. The game is detailed enough that Lucia and Jason will gain weight, their hair will grow long, and more. You can spend time truly focusing on your character’s appearance, and that is something I want out of my game of the year.

Recent findings suggest that let’s be honest, there are many games that are released that are buggy messes. For instance, massive games like Crimson Desert and Assassin’s Creed Shadows had some massive glitches that hurt the games when they were first released.

It took some rather large patches to fix them, and even then there were still issues. GTA 6 is one of the few games that have been released that has little to no issues with it, and in 2026, that is a massive feat, especially for a game with the the scope of GTA 6.

The lack of issues with the game at launch with how significant it is makes it a much more enticing pick for Game of the Year.

The Remnants Of The Electric Saab That Never Was Are Going Up For Auction

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I don’t really know why, but I’ve always been fascinated by Saab, the ill-fated Swedish car manufacturer.
  • In any case, the Saab car brand has been dead for precisely a decade, but now an auction is selling off a unique piece of automotive history that has deep ties to the now-defunct marque.
  • Sources indicate that the entire Emily GT project, which surfaced in 2023 after being developed in secrecy for half a decade, is being auctioned off in Sweden by Klaravik.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I don’t really know why, but I’ve always been fascinated by Saab, the ill-fated Swedish car manufacturer. Maybe it’s because it was always a little left-field, even when it was part of General Motors, or maybe I liked the cars’ design.

In any case, the Saab car brand has been dead for precisely a decade, but now an auction is selling off a unique piece of automotive history that has deep ties to the now-defunct marque.

Sources indicate that the entire Emily GT project, which surfaced in 2023 after being developed in secrecy for half a decade, is being auctioned off in Sweden by Klaravik. The lot includes a working mule prototype, bodies, parts, accessories, drawings, and four complete Emily GT prototypes, which are billed as the only ones that will ever be available on the open market.

Industry observers note that developed by ex-Saab engineers who worked at NEVS, the company that picked up the pieces after the storied automaker’s bankruptcy in 2012, the Emily GT was envisioned as a next-generation electric model with four in-wheel motors and a driving range of up to 600 miles, courtesy of a high-voltage battery that could, in theory, top out at 175 kilowatt-hours. According to technical drawings obtained by SaabPlanet, the standard-range car would have had a 105-kWh pack, while the mid-spec model was designed for a 140-kWh pack.

Wireless charging at up to 11 kW was also in the cards, and no fewer than four body styles, including a shooting brake, a sporty sedan, a two-door coupe, and a cabriolet.

Recent findings suggest that the four electric motors, developing a combined 490 horsepower, enabled a quite sophisticated torque vectoring system, leading to great road manners. However, none of it materialized. NEVS never had the cash to move forward with the project, and now all of the pieces are being sold off.

According to recent reports, “For us, this is a historic event, and I believe many Saab fans feel the same way,” stated Nina Selander, CEO of NEVS. “Despite only ever being built as a handful of prototypes, the Emily GT has achieved iconic status. That says a lot about the fascination with the car. By making the sale available in this way, we hope to attract car enthusiasts all over the world whose hearts beat for Saab.”.

Recent findings suggest that for the right buyer, it’s the perfect starter kit for a newly introduced car company, but it won’t come cheap. According to the Swedish local newspaper Ttela, the starting bid will be roughly $1.5 million (15 million SEK), and the auction house is not splitting the lot’s components into individual pieces. Everything is bundled into a single lot, so whoever has the highest bid goes home with everything.

Separately, Klaravik is auctioning off the world’s only NEVS Sango, a prototype of a self-driving vehicle designed for public transport that never materialized.

Both online auctions will go live on November 25 and will run through December 9.
